summary: Regime read: Tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 75% points tightening, 21% mixed, and 3% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (per U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics: Consumer Price Index News Release - 2026 M10 Results). Fed communications are strongly tightening (per Federal Reserve Board: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook). Employment is leaning tightening and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction, one vote per event cluster (no magnitude averaging)
scoring.clustering: one vote per event_key; representative = max-weight source; keyless sources are singleton clusters

sources.title: Why a CPI surprise could trip up the Fed's rate-cutting plans
sources.evidence_text: The article says an upside CPI surprise could push the Fed toward a pause in rate cuts and keep the policy rate unchanged at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation surprises higher, the Fed is more likely to delay easing to preserve credibility on price stability.

sources.title: Inflation edges up, highlighting Fed's bumpy path to stable prices
sources.evidence_text: The article says October CPI rose to 2.6% year over year, which it described as a bump that still likely would not change the Fed's near-term course.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer inflation print reduces the Fed's room to cut aggressively even if it does not fully reverse the easing cycle.

sources.title: Lower-Than-Expected Inflation Keeps Fed On Track For October Rate Cut
sources.evidence_text: The article says September CPI rose 3.0% year over year, below the expected 3.1%, and argues that this left the Fed on track for cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A downside inflation surprise reduces the immediate need for restraint and supports further easing if labor-market conditions also soften.

sources.title: Tame US inflation gives the Fed room for more rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: ING argued that softer November inflation gave the Fed more room to deliver additional cuts in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A clear disinflation surprise eases the constraint on the Fed's inflation mandate and supports more accommodation.

sources.title: CPI Surprises to the Downside
sources.evidence_text: The article says the latest CPI report came in well below expectations, which improved the odds of Fed rate cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer inflation surprise reduces pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive and supports additional easing.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates — November 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Treasury’s November 2 par-yield data showed the two-year constant-maturity yield at 4.59%.
sources.why_it_matters: Elevated two-year yields generally reflect expectations for a higher near-term policy-rate path, which argues against an easing regime.

sources.title: Economic News Releases
sources.evidence_text: September CPI rose 0.6% monthly and 3.7% annually, while core CPI rose 0.3% monthly and 2.6% annually.
sources.why_it_matters: The broad monthly increase and still-elevated core inflation provide limited room for faster policy easing.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims hover near 57-year lows
sources.evidence_text: Initial unemployment claims fell by 1,000 to 194,000 in the week ended October 24, while claims remained near multi-decade lows.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistently low layoffs indicate labor-market resilience, reducing the urgency for additional Federal Reserve cuts.

sources.title: US unemployment claims slide to 194,000, the lowest since mid-July
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims declined to 194,000, the four-week average fell to 196,750, and continuing claims decreased by 21,000 to about 1.7 million.
sources.why_it_matters: Broadly stable or improving claims data argues against labor-market deterioration that would prompt faster easing.

sources.title: FOMC October 29, 2026 Preview: Gold, Rate Odds & Key Data
sources.evidence_text: The reported December meeting pricing implied a substantially higher probability of a rate increase than a rate cut.
sources.why_it_matters: Market expectations for a hike rather than a cut signal that investors see the policy path drifting toward restraint.

sources.title: Fed Holds US Rate as S&P 500 Gains 0.3%
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve reportedly held the target range at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with two officials favoring a rate increase and inflation described as elevated.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold accompanied by dissenting votes for a hike and concern about elevated inflation indicates limited scope for near-term cuts.

sources.title: FOMC Statement
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve released an FOMC statement on October 28, 2026, but the available search result does not provide its policy decision or detailed wording.
sources.why_it_matters: The policy statement is the primary signal for whether labor-market risks and inflation conditions are shifting the reaction function toward additional easing or restraint.

sources.title: Quarterly Data Series on Business Employment Dynamics
sources.evidence_text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics listed the quarterly Business Employment Dynamics release among its October 28, 2026 releases, but the available result does not show the underlying employment changes.
sources.why_it_matters: Business births, deaths, and employment flows can alter the assessment of labor-market momentum, but the available evidence does not establish a clear easing or tightening signal.

sources.title: Metropolitan Area Employment and Unemployment
sources.evidence_text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics listed the September 2026 metropolitan employment and unemployment release on October 28, 2026, without details in the available result about the national labor-market signal.
sources.why_it_matters: Regional employment and unemployment data inform the Fed’s labor-market assessment, but no directional policy implication can be established from the available summary.

sources.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index
sources.evidence_text: The September 2026 PCE price index increased 3.6% from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August.
sources.why_it_matters: Accelerating headline PCE inflation leaves less room for rate cuts and strengthens the case for restrictive policy.

sources.title: CPI Home: Consumer Price Index
sources.evidence_text: September CPI rose 0.6 percent month over month and 3.7 percent over the year.
sources.why_it_matters: Elevated headline CPI momentum and annual inflation reduce the case for additional rate cuts.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board — Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve’s policy page identifies the October 28 FOMC statement and press conference as the latest monetary-policy communications and lists minutes for the October 27–28 meeting as forthcoming on November 18.
sources.why_it_matters: The October meeting’s official communication is the key baseline for judging whether subsequent labor-market information is shifting the easing or tightening regime.

sources.title: Personal Income and Outlays, September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The September PCE price index increased 0.5% month over month, while core PCE increased 0.3%; core PCE was 3.1% higher than a year earlier.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation remains materially above the Federal Reserve’s 2% objective, reducing scope for additional rate cuts.

sources.title: GDP, 3rd Quarter 2026 — Advance Estimate
sources.evidence_text: The GDP release reported quarterly PCE inflation of 2.1% and core PCE inflation of 2.5%.
sources.why_it_matters: Core inflation remains above target, supporting a cautious reaction function even though the quarterly readings are less acute than headline September PCE.

sources.title: U.S. Economy at a Glance
sources.evidence_text: September payroll growth was revised to a preliminary 29,000 increase, while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1% in August.
sources.why_it_matters: A cooling labor market reduces demand-driven inflation pressure and supports additional policy easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged despite elevated inflation
sources.evidence_text: The report said the Fed held rates amid elevated inflation and that markets priced nearly an 85% probability of another quarter-point increase at the December meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A market shift toward a hike rather than cuts signals that inflation risks are pushing expected policy in a tighter direction.

sources.title: Fed meeting live updates: Interest rates held steady in split vote
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC voted 10–2 to hold rates, with two officials dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point hike, while futures implied a higher probability of a December increase.
sources.why_it_matters: Hawkish dissents and increased near-term hike risk show policy risks have shifted away from cuts and toward further tightening.

sources.title: Fed meeting recap: Warsh says central bank will host fewer rate-setting ...
sources.evidence_text: The report describes September CPI inflation at 3.7% year over year, with core inflation at 3.1%, alongside a producer-price increase of 6.3% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation running materially above the 2% objective and showing renewed momentum argues against rapid cuts and raises the risk of additional restraint.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady as it awaits more information
sources.evidence_text: The Fed held rates steady, upgraded its assessment of economic growth to a strong pace, and said inflation remained elevated while awaiting additional data.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger growth alongside persistent inflation supports maintaining or increasing restriction rather than resuming an easing cycle.

sources.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as midterm elections loom
sources.evidence_text: The Fed left rates unchanged and indicated that policymakers were waiting for more economic data before deciding on the next policy move.
sources.why_it_matters: A data-dependent pause leaves the policy path open, although the elevated inflation backdrop limits immediate easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC voted 10–2 to keep the federal funds target range at 3.75%–4.00%, noting that job gains were keeping pace with the workforce, unemployment had changed little, and inflation remained elevated.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold amid stable labor conditions and elevated inflation indicates the Committee is not currently validating further cuts and retains a restrictive policy bias.

sources.title: October 27-28, 2026 FOMC Meeting
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC released its policy statement and implementation note following its October 27-28 meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: The policy decision is the primary reaction-function signal, but the available record does not establish a new cut or hike.

sources.title: US Fed Meeting Highlights: Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged
sources.evidence_text: The report described an unchanged policy rate, persistent inflation concerns, and no clear signal that the committee would cut or hike at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A data-dependent stance without easing guidance points to a continued restrictive regime.

sources.title: FOMC press conference, October 28, 2026
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The chair stressed the need to restore price stability while providing limited forward guidance after the decision to hold rates unchanged.
sources.why_it_matters: Emphasis on inflation control and uncertainty about the next move points away from an active cutting cycle.

sources.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady despite inflation concerns
sources.evidence_text: September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, while September payroll growth was only 29,000 and unemployment increased to 4.2%.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation materially above target argues against cuts, although weak hiring creates a competing reason to ease.

sources.title: Meeting calendars and information
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve calendar records the October 27–28, 2026 FOMC meeting and indicates that meeting minutes are released three weeks after the policy decision.
sources.why_it_matters: The calendar confirms the policy-event timing but does not yet provide evidence that the reaction function is shifting toward easing or tightening.

sources.title: TREASURIES-Short-term Treasury yields fall as Fed prompts rethink of rate-hike wagers
sources.evidence_text: The Fed held rates steady while markets still priced roughly a 78% probability of a December hike, and the two-year Treasury yield was about 4.68%.
sources.why_it_matters: A high probability of a near-term hike and an elevated two-year yield indicate markets expect policy to move away from easing.

sources.title: 10-year Treasury yield hovers below 5% after strong GDP ...
sources.evidence_text: The two-year Treasury yield fell more than 10 basis points to about 4.629% after the Fed held rates, while market commentary characterized the economy as strong, inflation as above target, and financial conditions as not restrictive.
sources.why_it_matters: The decline in the policy-sensitive yield offers modest easing evidence, but the reported macro assessment still supports keeping policy restrictive.

sources.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity
sources.evidence_text: FRED reports a 2-year Treasury constant-maturity yield of 4.61% for October 29, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The elevated 2-year yield embeds expectations of comparatively restrictive policy over the near-term horizon.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Outlook - Singapore
sources.evidence_text: The report said the FOMC held rates by a 10–2 vote and futures priced an approximately 85% probability of a 25-basis-point December hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A divided hold combined with high hike odds suggests the reaction function is biased toward further tightening rather than additional cuts.

sources.title: US Federal Reserve Keeps Rates Unchanged Despite Elevated Inflation
sources.evidence_text: The Fed kept its policy rate unchanged, described inflation as elevated, and indicated that it was waiting for more information before deciding its next step.
sources.why_it_matters: Holding rates amid elevated inflation preserves restrictive policy and leaves the next move more likely to be a hike than a cut.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady despite concerns over inflation
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch pricing cited in the report showed less than a 10% probability of a rate hike after the meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Limited immediate hike pricing means markets still expect a hold, but it does not support a strong easing signal and leaves policy risk skewed toward fewer cuts.

sources.title: Perspective: Morning Commentary for October 29
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch pricing indicated roughly an 83% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the December FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing for a hike at the next meeting indicates expectations are drifting away from easing and toward renewed tightening.

sources.title: Fed Policy Monitor: Supporting a timelier return to target
sources.evidence_text: The report said OIS markets assigned less than a 10% probability to an immediate follow-on hike after the October decision.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-term OIS pricing supports a pause rather than immediate tightening, although it does not establish an easing path.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady as it awaits accumulation of more information
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC held rates in a 3.75% to 4.00% range, described inflation as elevated, and upgraded its assessment of economic activity.
sources.why_it_matters: Elevated inflation alongside stronger activity supports maintaining restrictive policy and weighs against near-term easing.

sources.title: Treasury yields tick higher after Fed interest rate decision
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch showed an 85.7% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the December meeting, while the 2-year Treasury yield was about 4.704%.
sources.why_it_matters: A heavily priced near-term hike and elevated 2-year yield indicate markets expect restrictive policy rather than additional easing.

sources.title: Fed keeps interest rates unchanged, but two officials dissent
sources.evidence_text: Markets expected the Fed to hold rates in October, but the probability of a December hike rose to about 85% from 78% the previous day.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising odds of a December hike imply a meaningful shift away from an easing regime in the market-implied reaction function.

sources.title: Analysis—Fed highlights economic strength but muddies outlook
sources.evidence_text: Markets were pricing a possible December rate increase, while the Fed described economic conditions as strong enough for inflation to remain elevated.
sources.why_it_matters: Expectations of another hike indicate that the market reaction function is responding to persistent inflation and economic strength by delaying or reversing easing.

sources.title: BLS Weekly Update
sources.evidence_text: The October Employment Situation was scheduled for release on November 6, leaving the latest comprehensive payroll report as September data.
sources.why_it_matters: The absence of new payroll information limits the Fed's ability to update its reaction function from labor-market evidence.

sources.title: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims — October 29, 2026
sources.evidence_text: Initial unemployment claims fell to 194,000 in the week ending October 24, while the four-week average declined to 196,750.
sources.why_it_matters: Lower claims indicate continued labor-market resilience, but the modest decline in the moving average does not materially increase pressure for tighter policy.

sources.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, Excluding Food and Energy
sources.evidence_text: September 2026 core PCE inflation was 3.1% year over year, compared with 3.0% in August.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent underlying inflation remains materially above the 2% objective, arguing against near-term easing.

sources.title: Employment Cost Index Summary - 2026 Q03 Results
sources.evidence_text: The BLS released third-quarter 2026 Employment Cost Index data for the year ending in September 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Labor-cost momentum informs the Fed’s assessment of persistent inflation pressure, but the available result does not establish a clear easing or tightening signal.

sources.title: October Fed Meeting: Updates and Commentary
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve left its target range unchanged at 3.75%–4.00%, while futures pricing reportedly showed roughly a 90% probability of no December move and elevated expectations of a hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold combined with meaningful hike risk indicates markets are pricing less scope for additional easing and a tightening bias if inflation remains persistent.

sources.title: US inflation
sources.evidence_text: The coverage reported that September headline and core CPI accelerated to 3.7% annually and exceeded market expectations.
sources.why_it_matters: An upside inflation surprise would shift the reaction function toward holding rates higher for longer or tightening further.

sources.title: Employment Cost Index release schedule, third quarter 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics scheduled the third-quarter 2026 Employment Cost Index release for October 30, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The release timing identifies an upcoming labor-cost input but provides no observed wage-growth signal by itself.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady after hiking last meeting, with investors expecting more increases to come
sources.evidence_text: Market prices reflected an expected December hike and two additional increases over the following year, while the 2-year Treasury yield ended near 4.70%.
sources.why_it_matters: Expected multiple hikes and a high front-end yield imply markets see persistent inflation risk requiring tighter policy.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Rise Ahead of Federal Reserve Interest-Rate Decision
sources.evidence_text: Before the October decision, the 2-year Treasury yield was about 4.755% and markets assigned roughly a 91% probability to an unchanged policy rate, with a December hike nearly fully priced.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-term pricing favored a pause but strongly anticipated renewed tightening at the next meeting.

sources.title: US Short-Term Yields Fall as Traders Parse Warsh, Fed Path
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield fell about four basis points to 4.7% after the Fed held rates, even as traders retained approximately 90% odds of a December hike and reduced expectations for later increases.
sources.why_it_matters: December tightening remained likely, but the lower 2-year yield and reduced later-hike pricing indicate a somewhat less aggressive path.

sources.title: Kevin Warsh Vows No Ifs, Ands or Buts on Delivering Price Stability as Fed Holds Rates in October
sources.evidence_text: J.P. Morgan reports that consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year in September while economic growth remained resilient and the Fed emphasized price stability.
sources.why_it_matters: Above-target inflation combined with resilient activity gives the Fed less reason to prioritize further easing.

sources.title: H.15 - Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - November 06, 2026
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve reported a two-year Treasury yield of 4.46% on November 5, following readings between 4.56% and 4.61% during October 30 through November 4.
sources.why_it_matters: The elevated short-maturity yield reflects restrictive policy expectations, although the one-day decline modestly tempers the tightening signal.

sources.title: FOMC holds rates steady, markets mostly follow suit
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 decision, described inflation as elevated, and indicated that further hikes could depend on incoming inflation data.
sources.why_it_matters: A rate hold accompanied by elevated-inflation concerns and possible future hikes indicates that the reaction function remains biased against near-term easing.

sources.title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference, October 2026 FOMC Meeting
sources.evidence_text: The press conference characterized inflation as elevated and noted that household inflation expectations were above the Federal Reserve's 2 percent objective over at least the near term.
sources.why_it_matters: Above-target inflation and expectations raise the risk of persistence, reducing the scope for additional cuts.

sources.title: Metropolitan Area Employment and Unemployment (Monthly) News Release
sources.evidence_text: In September, unemployment rates were lower than a year earlier in 226 of 387 metropolitan areas, while payroll employment rose in only 11 areas and declined in 3.
sources.why_it_matters: The mixed geographic employment signal does not materially alter the national reaction-function assessment.

sources.title: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report
sources.evidence_text: Seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims fell to 189,000 in the week ending October 31, while the four-week average declined to 194,750.
sources.why_it_matters: Lower claims indicate continued labor-market resilience, reducing near-term pressure for additional Federal Reserve cuts.

sources.title: Employment Cost Index News Release - 2026 Q03 Results
sources.evidence_text: Civilian compensation costs rose 0.8% over the three months ending in September 2026, with wages and salaries up 0.7% and benefits up 0.9%.
sources.why_it_matters: Moderating but still positive compensation growth provides neither a strong labor-market cooling signal nor a clear inflationary wage shock for the Fed.

sources.title: Implementation Note issued October 28, 2026
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve issued an implementation note describing the operational decisions associated with the monetary-policy stance announced on October 28, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The operational note documents the current stance but does not, by itself, establish a directional shift toward further easing or tightening.

sources.title: FedWatch
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch provides probabilities for upcoming FOMC target-rate changes derived from 30-day Fed Funds futures.
sources.why_it_matters: Futures-implied probabilities indicate whether traders expect the next meeting to deliver a cut, no change, or a hike, but the available result does not report the current probability split.

sources.title: From the US Market Desk: AI Wobbles. Treasuries Step Up.
sources.evidence_text: The commentary reported a 2-year yield near 4.63%, a 79% futures-implied probability of a December hike, and expectations for another hike in March 2027.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher short-rate pricing and elevated hike probabilities imply markets were discounting fewer cuts and a more restrictive path.

sources.title: Economy Grows Faster as the Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady
sources.evidence_text: The commentary reported that the FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4.00% at its October meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: An unchanged policy rate preserves optionality and leaves the next move dependent on incoming inflation and activity data.

sources.title: USD/CAD technical outlook, central bank policies and NFP in focus
sources.evidence_text: As of November 1, market pricing indicated a 74.6% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the December 9 FOMC meeting versus a 25.4% probability of no change.
sources.why_it_matters: A dominant hike probability signals that markets expect policy to move away from easing at the next meeting.

sources.title: An Updated Outlook for Interest Rates in 2026 and 2027
sources.evidence_text: The analysis reports that the September projections shifted toward a 2026 federal funds rate range of 4.0%–4.4% and viewed a December quarter-point increase as plausible.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher projected policy rate raises the hurdle for cuts and supports a tightening interpretation of the reaction function.

sources.title: FOMC Statement: October 2026
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC left rates unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00%, with two members dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point hike.
sources.why_it_matters: Dissents for a hike reveal material upside pressure on the reaction function and reduce evidence that the Fed is in an active easing regime.

sources.title: US job openings increase sharply in September
sources.evidence_text: September job openings increased sharply, while economists surveyed by Reuters expected October payroll growth of 65,000 and an unemployment rate of 4.2 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: More vacancies and expected payroll improvement point to labor-demand resilience, potentially limiting the case for faster easing.

sources.title: Economic Update: Week of November 2, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The report said nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000, below an expected 90,000, and unemployment rose to 4.2%.
sources.why_it_matters: A weak employment gain and higher unemployment would reduce labor-market inflation pressure and support additional rate cuts, if confirmed by official data.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Regulatory Service
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points in September to 3.75%–4.00%, and the related administered rates were increased.
sources.why_it_matters: The enacted rate hike confirms that the policy regime had shifted toward tightening before the October pause.

sources.title: The Fed Is Suddenly on Hold. When Could It Start Hiking?
sources.evidence_text: The October FOMC reportedly held the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4% after a September hike, citing elevated inflation and a need for more information; market pricing assigned about a 76% probability to a December quarter-point hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A pause following a recent hike, combined with persistent inflation concerns and high subsequent-hike probabilities, is consistent with a tightening rather than easing reaction function.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Drops to 4.56%, Signaling Softer Fed Bets
sources.evidence_text: The two-year Treasury yield fell five basis points to 4.56% on November 2, suggesting somewhat softer expectations for the future policy rate.
sources.why_it_matters: A lower short-maturity yield can indicate reduced expectations for further hikes or a possible shift toward eventual cuts, partially offsetting the tightening signals.

sources.title: News about Fed
sources.evidence_text: Market expectations still favored a December rate increase, although the reported probability had declined to 76.6% from 80% over the prior week.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent pricing for a December hike supports fewer cuts or a tightening move despite some moderation in conviction.

sources.title: US Fed Funds Interest Rate: Latest Updates and Trends
sources.evidence_text: The cited November 2 FedWatch reading showed a 69.8% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase at the December 9 FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Pricing above 50% for a hike indicates that the expected near-term policy direction is tightening rather than easing.

sources.title: December 2026 Fed Combo · Rate and Dissents
sources.evidence_text: The source's market and model scenarios assigned their highest probabilities to a 25-basis-point December hike, with a hold as the next most likely outcome.
sources.why_it_matters: Both market and modeled scenarios place the modal near-term outcome on tightening rather than additional cuts.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Rates
sources.evidence_text: The Treasury data show the 2-year par yield at 4.74% on November 6, compared with 4.65% on November 2.
sources.why_it_matters: The increase in the 2-year yield over the week signals a market shift toward fewer expected cuts or more prospective tightening.

sources.title: Treasury Yields Little Changed in Asian Trade Ahead of Midterms, Key Data This Week
sources.evidence_text: The report said the 2-year yield rose to approximately 4.595% while investors awaited employment data and other policy-relevant releases.
sources.why_it_matters: A modest rise in the policy-sensitive 2-year yield suggests slightly firmer near-term rate expectations ahead of key data.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Nudge Higher as AI Fears Ebb
sources.evidence_text: The report said the 2-year yield rose 1.3 basis points and CME FedWatch put the chance of at least a 25-basis-point hike at the next meeting at 17.2%, down from 21% a week earlier and 57.6% a month earlier.
sources.why_it_matters: The lower hike probability offsets the modest yield increase and points to reduced tightening risk overall.

sources.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
sources.evidence_text: The minutes reported elevated inflation, a labor market viewed as near maximum employment with some recent strengthening, and unanimous support at the September meeting for a 25-basis-point rate increase to 3.75%–4.00%.
sources.why_it_matters: The combination of an enacted hike, elevated inflation, and limited employment slack indicates a clearly restrictive reaction function.

sources.title: Divided Fed Chooses Patience, Leaves Rates Unchanged
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept rates unchanged amid elevated inflation, while two policymakers preferred a 25-basis-point hike and officials described economic activity as strong.
sources.why_it_matters: A hawkish split and stronger activity assessment point toward fewer near-term cuts despite some labor-market cooling.

sources.title: Wage and Income Growth Expectations Before, During, and After the Pandemic Period
sources.evidence_text: A Federal Reserve research note examines the relationship between wage and income growth expectations and inflation expectations across the pandemic period.
sources.why_it_matters: The topic is relevant to inflation dynamics, but the research description alone does not establish a current directional policy signal.

sources.title: Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
sources.evidence_text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that a Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey release occurred on November 3, 2026, but the available result does not provide its figures.
sources.why_it_matters: Job openings and quits inform labor-market slack, yet the available evidence is insufficient to assess pressure for cuts or hikes.

sources.title: The Federal Reserve Isn't the Only Central Bank To Hike Rates in 2026
sources.evidence_text: J.P. Morgan reported that the Fed raised its target range to 3.75%–4.00% in September and that markets widely expected another quarter-point increase in December.
sources.why_it_matters: An already-delivered hike followed by expected further tightening shows policy has shifted away from an easing regime.

sources.title: What’s the Fed’s Next Move?
sources.evidence_text: J.P. Morgan reported that the October meeting held the target range at 3.75%–4.00% and forecast a 25-basis-point increase in December amid elevated inflation and resilient employment.
sources.why_it_matters: A projected near-term hike indicates that the baseline reaction function has moved away from immediate easing.

sources.title: Federal Funds Effective Rate
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED
sources.evidence_text: The effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on October 30, consistent with the current 3.75%–4.00% target range.
sources.why_it_matters: The rate confirms that policy remained restrictive and unchanged after the October meeting, without providing evidence of a new easing move.

sources.title: Quarterly Refunding Statement of the Assistant Secretary for Financial Markets
sources.evidence_text: The Treasury said quarterly financing would include regular bill auctions, cash-management bills, notes, bonds, TIPS, and two-year floating-rate notes.
sources.why_it_matters: Planned issuance can influence Treasury yields and term premiums, so the two-year yield should not be interpreted as a pure measure of Federal Reserve policy expectations.

sources.title: What to Expect From the October Jobs Report
sources.evidence_text: Ahead of the October release, consensus expectations called for roughly 59,000 payroll gains and a 4.2 percent unemployment rate, while private payroll data showed an 86,000 increase.
sources.why_it_matters: Expected stabilization after September's weak payroll gain would reduce the case for additional cuts, but the projected pace remains moderate and does not by itself imply renewed tightening.

sources.title: Employment Situation News Release - October 2026
sources.evidence_text: Nonfarm payroll employment increased by 165,000 in October, the unemployment rate was 4.1%, and average hourly earnings increased by $0.14.
sources.why_it_matters: Job gains above the prior-year average and continued low unemployment indicate resilient labor demand, reducing the urgency for additional policy easing.

sources.title: What To Expect From Friday's Jobs Report
sources.evidence_text: Economists surveyed ahead of the October jobs report expected about 59,000 payroll gains and an unemployment rate near 4.2%.
sources.why_it_matters: The forecast implied slower hiring but not a clearly deteriorating labor market, leaving the reaction-function signal mixed before the official release.

sources.title: FEDS 2026-071: How Firms Form Beliefs and the Implications for Inflation
sources.evidence_text: Federal Reserve research finds that firms' expectations of their own marginal costs can respond systematically to current and past costs while remaining disconnected from aggregate CPI expectations.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent firm cost expectations can sustain price-setting pressure, arguing for caution before further monetary easing.

sources.title: Current Employment Statistics
sources.evidence_text: The latest reported data show September payrolls up 29,000 and unemployment at 4.2%, with both little changed.
sources.why_it_matters: A stable labor market does not create a strong employment-based imperative for additional rate cuts, but it also does not signal substantial overheating.

sources.title: Fed's Hammack, Barkin favor gradual rate-hike path
sources.evidence_text: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin argued that policy should become restrictive or that inflation remains too high, while favoring gradual increases.
sources.why_it_matters: The officials’ comments reinforce a tightening bias, although their preference for gradual moves limits the signal for aggressive hikes.

sources.title: U.S. Financial Conditions: Tighter, But Not Tight
sources.evidence_text: TD Economics said markets moved from pricing two Fed cuts by year-end to anticipating 50 basis points of tightening by September 2027, with one additional hike as its baseline.
sources.why_it_matters: The removal of cuts and repricing toward hikes is a strong market signal that persistent inflation and firm activity are raising the expected policy path.

sources.title: Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - H.15
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve’s H.15 release reports the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.61% on November 3, following 4.59% on November 2 and 4.56% on October 30.
sources.why_it_matters: The short-maturity yield remains a market-based gauge of expected policy rates and is consistent with limited near-term easing.

sources.title: Employment Situation News Release - 2026 M10 Results
sources.evidence_text: Nonfarm payroll employment increased by 165,000 in October while the unemployment rate remained at 4.1 percent, and payroll growth exceeded the prior-12-month average.
sources.why_it_matters: Resilient hiring and a stable unemployment rate reduce the urgency for additional rate cuts, although they do not by themselves imply a need for hikes.

sources.title: Employment Situation News Release — October 2026
sources.evidence_text: Nonfarm payroll employment increased by 165,000 in October, while the unemployment rate was little changed at 4.1 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: Steady hiring and a stable unemployment rate indicate a resilient labor market, reducing the urgency for additional easing while not clearly requiring tighter policy.

sources.title: THE EMPLOYMENT SITUATION — OCTOBER 2026
sources.evidence_text: Nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 in October, unemployment remained at 4.1%, and employment growth exceeded the prior twelve-month average.
sources.why_it_matters: A stronger-than-expected labor market gives the Fed less reason to ease policy and supports a restrictive stance.

sources.title: US Treasuries Stumble as Strong Labor Market Lifts Fed-Hike Bets
sources.evidence_text: A stronger-than-expected US jobs report pushed the two-year Treasury yield up as much as seven basis points to 4.54%, while markets priced about a 70% chance of a quarter-point December rate hike.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger employment and higher near-term rate expectations reduce the case for cuts and increase pressure for additional tightening.

sources.title: Richmond Fed's Barkin Says he Expects More Rate Hikes But Unsure About How Many or When
sources.evidence_text: Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said he expected additional rate hikes, while the article reported a 76.2% probability of a hike in CME FedWatch pricing.
sources.why_it_matters: An FOMC participant signaling more hikes, alongside elevated market-implied hike odds, indicates policy is drifting toward tightening.

sources.title: Williams Says Fed Should Gather Data to Judge Price Risks
sources.evidence_text: New York Fed President John Williams endorsed waiting for more information to assess price risks, noting anchored inflation expectations and wage growth consistent with the 2% objective.
sources.why_it_matters: A data-dependent stance neither validates near-term cuts nor commits to hikes, leaving the reaction function dependent on incoming inflation and employment data.

sources.title: Key Interest Rates
sources.evidence_text: The two-year constant-maturity Treasury yield averaged 4.64% for the week ending October 30, compared with 4.74% the prior week and a 52-week low of 3.42%.
sources.why_it_matters: The weekly decline points to some easing in expected policy, but the yield remains substantially above its one-year low and therefore still reflects restrictive expectations.

sources.title: Employment Cost Index - September 2026
sources.evidence_text: Civilian compensation costs rose 3.4 percent over the year through September, with wages and salaries up 3.1 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent wage growth can sustain services inflation and make the Federal Reserve less willing to accelerate rate cuts.

sources.title: Inflation Hits Highest Since May as Energy Prices Surge
sources.evidence_text: BEA data showed September headline PCE inflation at 3.6% year over year and core PCE inflation at 3.1%, with both measures above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.
sources.why_it_matters: Elevated PCE inflation, especially core inflation, argues against near-term easing in the Fed's reaction function.

sources.title: October FOMC Decision: Fed on Hold, But Not Done
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4.00% after a September hike, while two members reportedly preferred another increase.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold following a recent hike, combined with dissenting calls for tighter policy, indicates limited commitment to an easing regime.

sources.title: Financial Markets
sources.evidence_text: The report said markets priced approximately an 85% probability of a 25-basis-point December rate hike after the October FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Pricing a likely hike represents a pronounced shift away from expectations for additional Fed cuts.

sources.title: October CPI Forecasts Show Inflation Softening, but December Rate Hike Still Looks Likely
sources.evidence_text: Economists expected October CPI inflation to slow from September but still viewed a December Fed rate increase as likely because inflation remained well above target.
sources.why_it_matters: A modest cooling that does not materially reduce expected tightening suggests the Fed's reaction function remains focused on persistent inflation.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board Calendar: November 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve calendar listed upcoming speeches by Vice Chair Jefferson, Governor Barr, Vice Chair Bowman, and Governor Waller, along with release of FOMC minutes.
sources.why_it_matters: The scheduled communications may alter expectations, but the calendar itself contains no new reaction-function signal.

sources.title: 2026 FOMC Press Releases
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve published an October 28, 2026 FOMC statement under its monetary-policy press releases.
sources.why_it_matters: An unchanged or non-easing policy communication indicates that the easing cycle is not being extended at this meeting.

sources.title: Report to the Secretary of the Treasury from the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee
sources.evidence_text: Treasury reported that markets had repriced toward a higher rate path, with two-year yields up roughly 50 basis points and approximately three additional rate increases priced over the following year.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher front-end yield curve and additional hikes priced into markets indicate substantially tighter expected monetary policy.

sources.title: Fed seen sticking to December rate hike after jobs data
sources.evidence_text: Markets were reported to price about a 78% probability of a quarter-point December hike after a stronger-than-expected October jobs report.
sources.why_it_matters: Resilient employment reduces the urgency for rate relief and gives the Fed more room to maintain or extend restrictive policy.

sources.title: US Fed rate hike in December faces uncertainty as jobs surge, but CPI and oil hold the key
sources.evidence_text: Market pricing assigns slightly less than an 80% probability to a 25-basis-point December rate increase, down from above 80%.
sources.why_it_matters: The next-meeting OIS-like policy signal still favors a hike, although declining conviction modestly reduces the tightening impulse.

sources.title: Midterm results may add uncertainty to the Fed's next rate decision
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch pricing indicated approximately a 76.8% probability of a 25-basis-point December hike as of November 6.
sources.why_it_matters: A market-implied probability above three-fourths suggests investors expect the Fed's next move to be tightening rather than easing.

sources.title: CIO Notebook: Fed Holds Rates Steady, Cites the Need for More Information
sources.evidence_text: Neuberger Berman judged a December hike highly probable even though it viewed the October meeting's tone as more dovish than September.
sources.why_it_matters: The combination of a dovish communication shift and strong near-term hike expectations points to a hawkish hold rather than renewed easing.

sources.title: Minutes of the Meeting of the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee
sources.evidence_text: The committee discussion attributed higher Treasury yields partly to stronger capex-driven growth and energy-price shocks that lifted real yields.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger growth and energy-related price pressure can reduce the scope for rate cuts and reinforce a restrictive policy stance.

sources.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook
sources.evidence_text: Governor Waller characterized the labor market as stable and near maximum employment while indicating support for a 25-basis-point policy-rate increase at the December meeting because inflation remains too high.
sources.why_it_matters: A policymaker viewing employment as near maximum and favoring a rate increase signals that labor-market conditions are not currently limiting the Fed’s ability to tighten.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index News Release - 2026 M10 Results
sources.evidence_text: Consumer prices increased 0.4% month over month in October 2026 after rising 0.6% in September, with shelter, food, and energy contributing to the increase.
sources.why_it_matters: The still-elevated monthly inflation pace and persistent service-price contribution argue for caution about additional rate cuts.

sources.title: Economic and monetary policy outlook
sources.evidence_text: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said inflation remains above target and indicated that at least two additional 25-basis-point rate increases are needed.
sources.why_it_matters: A regional Fed president explicitly favoring multiple further hikes signals that persistent inflation is shifting the reaction function toward tighter policy.

sources.title: Fed should move policy with care as it responds to inflation, Barkin says
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin identified inflation as the main risk and that investors expected a December rate increase.
sources.why_it_matters: Both inflation-focused Fed communication and reported market expectations point toward fewer cuts and a live tightening risk.

sources.title: Fed to Raise Rates Once More in December as Inflation Risks Stay High: Reuters Poll
sources.evidence_text: A November Reuters survey found all 101 economists expected a December hike, while 45 still expected at least two further increases.
sources.why_it_matters: Consensus expectations for a December hike and a meaningful tail for additional hikes indicate that easing is not the prevailing near-term policy scenario.

sources.title: Economic Outlook: Economy keeps on keeping on
sources.evidence_text: U.S. Bank projected additional 25-basis-point increases in December and March, with risks tilted toward a longer tightening cycle.
sources.why_it_matters: The forecast provides an external scenario consistent with persistent inflation and resilient demand delaying any return to an easing regime.

sources.title: 10-year Treasury yield races back to 5% as inflation data, Waller comments drive rate hike expectations
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield rose more than 15 basis points to 4.698% as markets increased expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes.
sources.why_it_matters: A sharp rise in the policy-sensitive 2-year yield indicates markets are pricing less easing and greater risk of additional tightening.

sources.title: Treasury yields rise as investors await October CPI and ...
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield climbed as strong employment data and anticipated inflation data led investors to reassess the future path of Federal Reserve policy.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher short-maturity yields reflect reduced confidence in near-term cuts and a more restrictive expected policy path.

sources.title: Fed's Waller plans to support at least a quarter-point rate ...
sources.evidence_text: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller indicated support for at least a quarter-point December rate increase and said a larger hike could be considered if inflation worsens.
sources.why_it_matters: A stated preference for renewed rate increases directly shifts the reaction function away from easing and toward tightening.
